subject: physics
title: Energy stores and systems
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Energy stores and systems — AQA GCSE Physics (8463) specification, section 4.1.1.1.
meta_desc: GCSE Physics (AQA) practice covering Energy stores and systems, specification section 4.1.1.1.
final_note: You worked through Energy stores and systems — 13 specification statements.

concepts.def: A system is an object or a group of objects. It is simply whatever you choose to treat as the thing being studied — a single stone, a stone and the Earth together, or a kettle together with the water inside it. Choosing the system first is what makes it possible to say clearly which stores are emptying and which are filling.

A way in which a system holds energy. Naming a store answers the question 'where is the energy now?' — for example the kinetic store, the gravitational potential store, the elastic potential store, the thermal store and the chemical store.
The store filled when an object moves. The faster the object moves and the greater its mass, the more energy is in its kinetic store.
The store filled when an object is raised. Its content depends on the mass of the object, its height, and the gravitational field strength.
The store filled when an object such as a spring, a rubber band or a crumpling car bumper is stretched, squashed or deformed.
The store filled when the temperature of a material rises. Almost every everyday change ends with energy in the thermal stores of the objects involved and of the surroundings.
The store held in fuels, foods and batteries, which empties when a chemical reaction such as burning or respiration takes place.
The moving of energy from one store to another. A transfer is not itself a store: the routes named in this section are heating, work done by forces and work done when a current flows.
A transfer of energy caused by a difference in temperature. Heating fills the thermal store of the cooler object and empties the store supplying the energy.
The transfer of energy that happens when a force moves an object through a distance along the line of the force. Work done is calculated using W = F s.

concepts.term: Work done when a current flows
concepts.def: The transfer of energy that happens when charge is pushed through a component by a power supply. The energy transferred in a time t is found from P = E / t.
The spreading out of energy into thermal stores of the surroundings, where it is no longer useful. The energy is still there; it is simply shared out too thinly to be used.
A diagram in which the energy in each store, before and after a change, is drawn as a bar using the same scale throughout, so that the redistribution of a fixed total can be seen at a glance.

mcqs.q: In physics, what is meant by a system?
options: An object, or a group of objects, being studied.
A machine that has been built to move energy.
A group of two or more objects, never one.
A place where energy is kept until used.
mcqs.explain: This is the specification's definition: a system is an object or group of objects.

mcqs.q: What always happens when a system changes?
options: Some of the energy in the system is used up.
The way energy is stored in the system changes.
The amount of energy in the system rises.
Extra energy is created inside the system itself.
mcqs.explain: This is exactly what the specification says happens when a system changes.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a way of storing energy rather than a way of transferring it?
options: The heating of a large beaker of cold water.
The work done by a steady pushing force.
The elastic store of a squashed spring.
An electric current in a copper wire.
mcqs.explain: A stretched or squashed spring holds energy, so this is a store.

mcqs.q: The specification asks for all the changes in the way energy is stored when a system changes. What must such a description name?
options: Only the store that empties during the change.
Only the useful store that fills in the change.
The size of the force that is acting on the system.
Each store that empties and each that fills.
mcqs.explain: 'All the changes' means both ends of every transfer are named.

mcqs.q: A ball is thrown straight upwards. As it rises, what happens to the way energy is stored?
options: The gravitational store empties, the kinetic store fills.
The kinetic store empties and the gravitational store fills.
The kinetic store keeps filling while the ball rises.
Both the kinetic and the gravitational stores fill.
mcqs.explain: The ball slows as it gains height, so the kinetic store empties into the gravitational store.

mcqs.q: Air resistance is ignored. At the highest point of a ball's flight, what has happened to the energy that was in its kinetic store?
options: It was destroyed at the moment the ball stopped.
It has been transferred to the elastic store of the air.
Some remains, because the ball is still moving up.
It has all been transferred to the gravitational store.
mcqs.explain: With no air resistance the whole of the kinetic store fills the gravitational store.

mcqs.q: A trolley moving along a bench hits a wall and stops. What happens to the energy in its kinetic store?
options: It is transferred to thermal stores and by sound.
It is destroyed by the impact of the trolley on the wall.
It is used up in bringing the trolley to a stop.
It stays in the kinetic store of the stopped trolley.
mcqs.explain: The trolley, the wall and the surrounding air warm slightly and a sound wave carries some energy away.

mcqs.q: A constant horizontal force pushes a box along a smooth, level floor. Which store fills as the box speeds up?
options: The gravitational store of the moving box.
The chemical store of the pushing force.
The kinetic store of the moving box.
The elastic store of the smooth floor.
mcqs.explain: Work done by the force transfers energy to the kinetic store as the box speeds up.

mcqs.q: A car slows down when the driver brakes. Which statement describes the changes in the way energy is stored?
options: The kinetic store empties into the chemical store of the brakes.
Energy is lost from the car, so the total energy falls.
The kinetic store empties and the thermal stores of the brakes fill.
The gravitational store of the car fills as the car slows.
mcqs.explain: Friction at the brakes does work, filling thermal stores of the brakes, tyres, road and air.

mcqs.q: A cyclist stops pedalling on level ground and slowly freewheels to a stop. Which store empties?
options: The kinetic store of the cyclist and the bicycle.
The chemical store held in the cyclist's leg muscles.
The gravitational store of the moving bicycle.
The thermal store of the road and the air.
mcqs.explain: Friction and air resistance do work, emptying the kinetic store into thermal stores.

mcqs.q: Water is brought to the boil in an electric kettle. Which statement describes the main change in the way energy is stored?
options: The chemical store of the kettle itself empties into the water.
The water gains a store of electrical energy as it is heated.
The kinetic store of the water fills as the water boils.
The current does work and the water's thermal store fills.
mcqs.explain: A current in the element does work; the thermal stores of the element and then the water fill.

mcqs.q: As well as the water, which other thermal stores fill while a kettle boils?
options: Only the water's store; nothing else becomes warm.
Those of the kettle and of the air around it.
None, because the water uses up all the energy.
Those of the mains cable and the power supply.
mcqs.explain: The element, the kettle body and the surrounding air all end up warmer.

mcqs.q: 0.50 kg of water is heated from 20 °C to 90 °C. The specific heat capacity of water is 4200 J/kg °C. Using ΔE = m c Δθ, what is the change in thermal energy?
A heater is switched on under a beaker of water. What does heating the water do?
options: It raises its temperature but transfers no energy.
It fills the kinetic store of the beaker.
It transfers energy to the water's thermal store.
It uses up energy inside the water each second.
mcqs.explain: Heating is a transfer route, and the store it fills is the thermal store of the water.

mcqs.q: A constant force of 40 N pushes a crate 2.5 m across a floor, in the direction of the force. Using W = F s, how much work is done?
A constant force does work on a moving object along the line of the force. What does this work do?
options: It fills the kinetic store of the object.
It is stored as force inside the moving object.
It uses up the energy the object already has.
It fills up the gravitational store instead.
mcqs.explain: Work done by a resultant force along the motion transfers energy to the kinetic store.

mcqs.q: A 2000 W kettle is switched on for 90 s. Using P = E / t, how much energy is transferred by the current?
mcqs.explain: P = E / t rearranges to E = P t, so E = 2000 × 90 = 180 000 J.

mcqs.q: A current flows through the heating element of a hairdryer. Which statement is correct?
options: The element holds a store of electrical energy inside itself.
The current is used up as it passes through the element.
The current does work, filling the element's thermal store.
The chemical store of the metal wire empties into it.
mcqs.explain: Work done when a current flows is the transfer route; the thermal store fills.

mcqs.q: An energy diagram drawn to a common scale shows the stores in a system before and after a change. What must be true of the bars?
options: The total after the change must be smaller than before.
Every bar after the change matches a bar before it.
The useful output bar must equal the input bar.
The bars after the change add to the same total.
mcqs.explain: A common scale shows the same total redistributed between different stores.

mcqs.q: A lamp is supplied with 500 J of energy. It transfers 60 J to the surroundings by light. Drawn on a common scale, what must the remaining bar show?
options: 560 J, the two amounts added together.
440 J, going to thermal stores.
60 J, the same as the light output.
Nothing, the energy has been used up.
mcqs.explain: 500 − 60 = 440 J, which fills thermal stores of the lamp and the surroundings.
